name: Structured Chain-of-Thought for Code Generation
executive_summary: Impose program-structure-aware intermediate reasoning (branches, loops) for code-generation tasks, instead of free-text CoT that ignores the target language's actual control-flow structure.
description: Adapts chain-of-thought specifically to code generation by having the intermediate reasoning steps mirror program structures (conditionals, loops) that the final code will actually contain, rather than generic natural-language reasoning. Machine-checkable via test execution, unlike most reasoning-elicitation techniques.
when_to_use: Code-generation tasks where a test suite or execution harness can verify correctness.
when_not_to_use: Non-code generation tasks, or code-generation with no way to execute/verify output.
known_pitfalls: Benefit is language- and task-dependent; structured reasoning helps most where target control-flow is genuinely nontrivial.

primary_source.title: Structured Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Code Generation

usage_templates.template:
Task: {{coding_task}}
Before writing code, outline the control-flow structure you will use (loops, conditionals, function boundaries) as pseudocode-level structured reasoning, not prose. Then write the actual {{target_language}} code implementing that structure.
usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
